title: Aph. V-VIII: contents of Pentateuch, Triteuch, Octateuch; poetic books
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss: See there chapter 11 on the poetic books entire. The poetic follow, that same which stand as the most elegant practice plus epitome belonging toward the law plus the prophets — as Job, the Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, the Song belonging toward Songs. And these stand as the historical books belonging toward the ancient Hebrew canon. VIII. 14-15 plus following through 23. See there Aph. the two belonging toward Kings, the two belonging toward Chronicles, the book belonging toward Ezra plus Nehemiah, plus the book belonging toward Esther — the two belonging toward Samuel. The Octateuch stands as that same that which contains the eight following books: VII. 11-13. See there Aph. The Triteuch embraces three books, namely Joshua, Judges, plus Ruth. VI. 6-10. Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy — on that same which see Contracted Theology book 1 chapter 9 Aph — the Pentateuch contains Genesis. V.
pass_b_english: V. The Pentateuch contains Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy — on which see Contracted Theology book 1 chapter 9 Aph. 6-10.
VI. The Triteuch embraces three books, namely Joshua, Judges, and Ruth. See there Aph. 11-13.

VII. The Octateuch is that which contains the eight following books: the two of Samuel, the two of Kings, the two of Chronicles, the book of Ezra and Nehemiah, and the book of Esther. See there Aph. 14-15 and following through 23.

VIII. And these are the historical books of the ancient Hebrew canon. The poetic follow, which are the most elegant practice and epitome of the law and the prophets — as Job, the Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, the Song of Songs. See there chapter 11 on the poetic books entire.
source_text: V. Pentateuchus continet Genesin, Exodum, Leviticum, Numeros, Deuteronomium: de quibus vide Theologiam contractam lib. 1. c. 9. aph. 6.7.8.9.10. VI. Triteuchus tres libros, nempe Josue, Judicum & Ruth complectitur. Vide ibidem Aph. 11.12.13. VII. Octateuchus est, qui continet octo sequentes libros, duos Samuelis, Regum duos, duos Chronicorum, librum Esrae & Nehemiae, librumque Estherae. vide ibidem aph. 14.15. & seqq. usque ad 23. VIII. Et hi sunt libri historici antiqui Hebraeorum canonis: Sequentur poetici, qui sunt elegantissima legis prophetarumque praxis et epitome, ut Jobus, Psalmi, Proverbia, Ecclesiastes, Canticum canticorum. Vide ibidem c. 11. de libris poeticis totum.
